1.title: The Product and Service Lifecycle and the Value Chain
1.text: Welcome to Module five: The Product and Service Lifecycle and the Value Chain. It covers the exam area The eye til Product and Service Lifecycle. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. List the eight lifecycle activities. Understand the lifecycle. Understand that the activities are not sequential or linear and can be used iteratively. Define the value chain. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The eye til Product and Service Lifecycle (ten percent). Exam format: forty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; twenty-six correct answers (sixty-five percent) pass. Validated against: the official eye til Foundation (Version five) syllabus, version five point zero (February two thousand twenty-six).

1.title: The eight activities
1.text: The eight activities. The eye til Product and Service Lifecycle is a model of eight activities that apply to every product and service. Discover to Design to Acquire to Build to Transition to Operate to Deliver to Support.

1.title: The eight activities, continued
1.text: The eight activities. The figure shows this: The eight lifecycle activities arranged as a loop, not a straight line.

1.title: The eight activities, continued
1.text: The eight activities. Discover. Find out what consumers need and what is possible. Design. Turn needs into specifications and prototypes. Acquire. Get the people, tools and components needed. Build. Create, configure and test the product or service. Transition. Move it safely into live use. Operate. Run it so it performs as agreed. Deliver. Provide the service to consumers. Support. Restore normal operation and help users. Exam tip: The list has eight items, in this order. A common distractor is an eye til four word such as plan, improve or engage; those belong to the old six-activity service value chain.

1.title: Not sequential, not linear
1.text: Not sequential, not linear. The activities are not a waterfall. Work loops, overlaps and repeats: a support finding can send you back to discover or design, and teams may run several activities in parallel. Use them iteratively, a little at a time, with feedback. Not every organization performs all eight: a provider that builds nothing still discovers, transitions, operates, delivers and supports.

1.title: Not sequential, not linear, continued
1.text: Not sequential, not linear. More product work. discover, design, acquire, build. The bridge. transition, operate. More service work. deliver, support. Products and services are two sides of the same digital solution, so the lifecycle covers both.

1.title: The value chain
1.text: The value chain. The value chain is the operating model of the lifecycle activities: the flow of activities that an organization performs to turn demand into value through products and services. It is one of the five components of the eye til Value System (Module eight). In eye til four the service value chain had six activities: plan, improve, engage, design and transition, obtain or build, deliver and support. Version five simplified this and uses the eight-activity lifecycle. If a question names the six old activities, it is using eye til four language. Exam tip: The lifecycle is not a waterfall. Any option that says the activities must be completed once, in strict order, is wrong.

1.title: The value chain, continued
1.text: The value chain. Exam tip: Count eight. If an option lists six activities with words such as plan or improve, it describes the eye til four value chain.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which list shows the eye til Product and Service Lifecycle activities? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Discover, design, acquire, build, transition, operate, deliver, support. Option A is the eye til four value chain; option B is the Version five lifecycle.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which statement about the lifecycle activities is C O R R E C T? (one) They are not strictly sequential. (two) They can be used iteratively. (three) They must always be completed in order, one at a time. (four) They apply only to physical goods. The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: one and two. The activities are not sequential or linear and can be iterated.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A managed service provider builds no software but runs and supports a client's platform. Which statement fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: It performs only the activities that apply to it, such as transition, operate, deliver and support. Not every organization performs every activity.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Identify the missing word(s). Products and services are blank of the same digitally enabled solution. The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Two sides. eye til treats them as two sides of the same solution.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An engineer finds a defect in live support and the team revisits the design. What does this show? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The lifecycle activities can loop back and be used iteratively. Activities can loop and repeat.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which activity sits between "build" and "operate"? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Transition. The order is build, transition, operate.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How many lifecycle activities are there in Version five? Answer: Eight. Question two. Name the eight activities in order. Answer: Discover, design, acquire, build, transition, operate, deliver, support. Question three. Are the activities strictly sequential? Answer: No; they are not sequential or linear and can be used iteratively.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What did eye til four call the six-activity flow? Answer: The service value chain. Question five. Which activity restores normal operation and helps users? Answer: Support. Question six. What is the value chain? Answer: The flow of activities that turns demand into value through products and services.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Eight activities: discover, design, acquire, build, transition, operate, deliver, support. Shape: not sequential or linear; iterative. Product or service lean: discover-build or deliver-support; transition and operate bridge. Old wording: six-activity eye til four service value chain.
